chapter: Blue Devils, Moten and the Reno Club
title: Jimmy Rushing as his right arm; Cherry Blossom club
summary: Kuehl reads a quote about Rushing urging Basie to keep the band going, and Jo Jones recalling the Cherry Blossom, where a piano was rolled on the floor.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: 'In all the time he was with the band, Jimmy Rushing has been what I might call my right arm.' You said that? 'There were times in the early days of the band that I'd have given it all up but for Jimmy's urging me to stick with it.'
You'll just let that remain there (inaudible).
Okay. Your point is well taken.
Now, this is Joe talking. "We worked with Basie at a place called the Cherry Blossom."
"They used to have a piano they would roll on the floor and Jimmy Rushing would go around serenading the people."
"Now Marylou --" well, I won't give you this, because --
-- Joe talking. "The second Basie band I was with started in '36 as a small combo and it went up from seven to nine to ten to 14." From seven to nine to ten to 14?
